{{short description|German mathematician}}
[[File:ErnstAugustWeissPortrait.jpg|thumb|From Strubecker's obituary<ref name="Strubecker.1943">{{cite journal | author=Karl Strubecker |author-link=:de:Karl Strubecker | title=Ernst August Weiss | journal=[[Deutsche Mathematik]] | volume=7 | number=2/3 | pages=254–298 | date=July 1943 }}</ref>]]
'''Ernst August Weiß'''<ref name="Blaschke.1942">{{cite journal | author=Blaschke, W. | author-link=Wilhelm Blaschke| title=E. A. Weiß † | journal=[[Jahresbericht der Deutschen Mathematiker-Vereinigung]] | volume=52 | pages=174–176 | url=http://www.digizeitschriften.de/download/PPN37721857X_0052/log20.pdf | year=1942 }}</ref>  (or '''Weiss''';<ref name="Strubecker.1943"/> 5 May 1900 in [[Strasbourg]] – 9 February 1942 in a Nazi [[field hospital]] near [[Lake Ilmen]]) was a German mathematician.

==Early life and education==
Since 1906, he attended the [[Lyceum]] in [[Metz]], the Luther school and (1910–1912) Schiller [[Gymnasium (Germany)|gymnasium]] in [[Münster]], and 1912–1917 the [[Mommsen-Gymnasium]] in [[Berlin]], where he passed the [[Notabitur]]. He volunteered for the German [[military engineers]] in [[World War I]], participated in the [[attrition warfare]] near [[Reims]] and [[Soissons]] and was captured 26 September 1918 during the tank battle near [[Cheppy]] by American soldiers.<ref name="Strubecker.1943"/>{{rp|255}}
After his release in September 1919 he studied mathematics at [[Leibniz University Hannover]] and (1920–1924) [[Bonn University]], where he obtained a [[Ph.D.#Germany|Ph.D.]] in March 1924<ref name="Strubecker.1943"/>{{rp|256}} and a [[Habilitation#Germany|habilitation]] in May 1926.<ref name="Strubecker.1943"/>{{rp|257}} 
In August 1926, he married the physicist Eva Renate Bidder.<ref>[http://www.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/helios/fachinfo/www/math/akademie/Weiss.htm Record] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180404135833/http://www.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/helios/fachinfo/www/math/akademie/Weiss.htm |date=2018-04-04 }} at [[University Heidelberg]] library</ref>

==Work in SA==
Weiß joined an [[Sturmabteilung|SA storm]] in [[Bonn]] in 1933, and got promoted up to an [[SA-Obertruppführer|Obertruppführer]]. He directed the Bonn [[Studentenwerk]].<ref name="Strubecker.1943"/>{{rp|260}} He created the Mathematical Work Camps ("Mathematische Arbeitslager") in [[Kronenburg (Eifel)|Kronenburg]] "as a new form of mathematical university teaching and collaboration of professors and students",<ref name="Strubecker.1943"/>{{rp|261}} which took place 1&mdash;15 March 1934, 15&mdash;29 October 1934, 17 February&ndash;3 March 1935,<ref>{{cite journal | author=Fritz Kubach |author-link=:de:Fritz Kubach | title=Mathematische Arbeitslager | journal=Deutsche Mathematik | volume=1 | number=1 | pages=12–14 | date=January 1936 }}</ref> 23 February&ndash;7 March 1936,<ref>{{cite journal | author=E.A. Weiß and Matth. Theis | title=Das vierte Mathematische Arbeitslager in Kronenburg (Eifel) | journal=Deutsche Mathematik | volume=1 | number=3 | pages=265–269 | date=July 1936 | title-link=Kronenburg (Eifel) }}</ref> and 17&mdash;31 October 1938.<ref>{{cite journal |author=<!-- No author --> |title=Arbeiten aus dem 5. Mathematischen Arbeitslager Kronenburg |journal=Deutsche Mathematik |volume=4 |issue=2 |date=May 1939| pages=247–272}}</ref>
Segal (1992) examined Weiß' camps from a pedagogical point of view, "as one example of how mathematics and Nazi ideology would interact".<ref>{{cite book | author=Sanford L. Segal | author-link=Sanford L. Segal| contribution=Ernst August Weiss: Mathematical Pedagogical Innovation in the Third Reich | pages=693–704| editor1=Sergei S. Demidov | editor2= Menso Folkerts |editor2-link=Menso Folkerts | editor3= David E. Rowe | editor-link3= David E. Rowe |display-editors = 3 |editor4= Christoph J. Scriba | editor-link4=Christoph Scriba| title=Amphora &mdash; Festschrift for Hans Wussing on the Occasion of his 65th Birthday | location=Basel | publisher=Springer | isbn=978-3-0348-9696-2 | year=1992 | doi=10.1007/978-3-0348-8599-7}}</ref>
Weiß was a permanent editor of the journal ''[[Deutsche Mathematik]]''.
A list of his publications is given in Blaschke (1942).<ref name="Blaschke.1942"/>

==Death==
In 1941, Weiß took part in [[Operation Barbarossa]] as [[company commander]] of an [[Military engineering|engineer]] unit; during the [[Demyansk Pocket]] he was mortally wounded in close combat in Lukinn.<ref name="Strubecker.1943"/>{{rp|263}}
